extracted.intended_audience: artists seeking residency opportunities, alumni, donors, and visitors
extracted.subtask_description: Information about the Ucross Foundation residency program — what the program offers, who it serves (disciplines, Indigenous fellowships), and the kinds of facilities, time, and community residents can expect. Useful for artists considering or preparing an application or stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program mission / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of Ucross Foundation is to foster the creative spirit of working artists and groups by providing uninterrupted time, studio space, living accommodations, and the experience of the majestic High Plains while serving as a responsible steward of its historic 20,000-acre ranch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement defines what the residency is intended to provide to applicants: protected time and place for creative work, specific on-site resources (studios, residences), and an aesthetic/environmental experience (the High Plains). It signals program priorities (uninterrupted work time and stewardship of the land) that applicants should reference when explaining fit or need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplines accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross serves artists from all disciplines, including literature, visual arts, music, choreography, film, performance, and multidisciplinary art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is explicitly multidisciplinary; applicants across these named fields (and related interdisciplinary practices) are within scope. Use this to determine eligibility/fit and to tailor application materials to reflect disciplinary practice and how time at Ucross would support that work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency environment and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Visiting artists receive private studios and residences and build a small, intense community while working in the midst of 20,000 acres of Wyoming ranchland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The emphasis on private studio/residence and an intense, small community suggests expectations about solitary work time balanced with peer interaction. Applicants should articulate how they would use uninterrupted studio time and how they engage (or not) with a small cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for Native American / Indigenous artists
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross runs Native American Fellowships and exhibitions highlighting Indigenous artists (e.g., the Ucross Fellowship for Native American Artists and related gallery exhibitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation provides targeted fellowship opportunities and programming for Indigenous artists; Indigenous applicants or those working with Indigenous communities should look for specific fellowship pages and may emphasize cultural relevance, community impact, or contributions to Indigenous artistic resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and on-site resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The campus includes named facilities/studios (Kocur, Rock Studios, School House & Depot, Jesse's One and Two, Dance Studio), an art gallery, café, Raymond Plank Center, chapel, gardens, and public park space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note available facilities when proposing projects that require particular spaces (e.g., dance studio, visual art studios) and describe any special needs. The presence of a gallery and public spaces also suggests opportunities (and possible expectations) for public-facing events or exhibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public programming and community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross hosts public events (Founder's Day with open studios and artist visits, artist talks, receptions, festivals, sound hikes, yoga in the park) and the gallery is open to the public with scheduled exhibitions and artist talks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the program emphasizes uninterrupted work time, the site indicates occasions when artists participate in public programming (open studios, talks, receptions). Applicants should clarify availability/interest in public engagement and whether they can or wish to participate in scheduled public events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni network and publication/press visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross highlights selected honors & notable alumni, press (NYT, Hyperallergic, regional press), a cookbook co-authored by alumni, and alumni news, indicating an active alumni community and public visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may reference alumni outcomes or community when articulating how Ucross residency will advance their career. The program's publicity channels can offer opportunities for visibility; applicants might indicate how residency could be leveraged for dissemination or career development.
